top_violation_types.title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022, as required.

top_violation_types.title: Fenced Outdoor Activity Space -Exits Required (26 TAC §746.4307)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: On the infant/toddler playground they is only one exit, the fence area needs another exit.

top_violation_types.title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation knowingly allowed persons to be present at the operation before receiving notification from the CBCU that the persons eligibility determination is Eligible, Provisional or Eligible with Conditions.

top_violation_types.title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Training records were not available for review.

top_violation_types.title: Franchise Tax Delinquent (26 TAC §745.247)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: According to the Texas Comptroller website, the business entity's Franchise Tax Account Status is Inactive/Forfeited. The operation is currently providing care to children with an inactive status.

top_violation_types.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))
AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation, it was determined that the staff was aware of a child receiving medical attention after sustaining an injury while in care, but did not report to Child Care Licensing within two days of becoming notified.

top_violation_types.title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - No Foods That Present Choking Risk (26 TAC §746.3317(7))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During an investigation it was found that a caregiver gave a toddler Mike and Ike candy which can be a choking hazard for that age group. The caregiver no longer works at the operation.
